note: Learning metadata only. These objects do not authorize, deny, or detect. Splunk does not enforce CTRL-MCP-001.
path_a: TRY IT YOURSELF — construct the search in Splunk Search. Studio tokens are not the fresh LIVE run.id.
path_b: SHOW SOLUTION — copyable SPL from an existing Q-MCP hunt, bound table on canonical REPLAY, explanation, limitations.

investigations.title: Find the run
investigations.security_question: Can you reconstruct the events that belong to this experiment?
investigations.learning_objective: Use run.id as the forensic correlation key. One UUID, one experiment copy.
prerequisites: a run.id from Attack Service or Investigate specimen
investigations.starter_guidance: Index agentsec_telemetry, sourcetype otel:agentic:json. Filter quoted agentsec.run.id. Do not search index=*. Then name the principal, agent, and tool.
investigations.hint_1: Start with index=agentsec_telemetry sourcetype=otel:agentic:json and the quoted field agentsec.run.id. Paste the LIVE run.id from Attack Service, or use the Investigate specimen REPLAY id.
investigations.hint_2: Q-MCP-WHO is the governed hunt for principal / agent / tool on control.decision. Count physical events with stats dc(_raw) as n. Do not use stats count by agentsec.run.id.
investigations.expected_result_shape: One control.decision identity row per run. LIVE ATTACK (vulnerable) and BASELINE also have mcp.* rows in the copy. Defended RETEST has control.decision and no mcp.started. Canonical REPLAY schema on this volume may be 1.1.0; fresh LIVE after restage is 1.9.0.
investigations.result_explanation: You are looking at the indexed copy of one MCP invoke. run.id is the experiment key. tool is what was requested, not what was granted.
investigations.security_interpretation: Correlation starts with run.id. Without it you mix experiments. Rows in Splunk are a copy of telemetry, not an authorization decision.
investigations.does_not_prove: Index presence does not prove completeness, prevention, or that the handler ran. Empty is not SAFE.
investigations.related_control: none on this step — you are locating evidence, not judging CTRL-MCP-001 yet

investigations.title: Find the tool request
investigations.security_question: What tool, scope, and resource did the agent request?
investigations.learning_objective: Separate request fields from grant fields. requested_scope is not allowed_scope.
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep the same run.id. Read gen_ai.tool.name, agentsec.mcp.requested_scope, and argument preview/hash. Do not expect gen_ai.tool.call.arguments to be fully indexed.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-WHO names the tool. Q-MCP-PARAMS shows argument preview and hash. Q-MCP-SCOPE compares requested_scope to coded allowed_scope.
investigations.hint_2: ATTACK and RETEST should request lookup_customer_tier / customer:read / customer_id=cust-001. BASELINE requests lookup_policy / policy:read. The request is not the grant.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK/RETEST: tool lookup_customer_tier. BASELINE: lookup_policy. Scope relation is requested vs allowed, not a grant mutation.
investigations.result_explanation: These fields are the request the runtime hashed. They are not a new allow-list.
investigations.security_interpretation: REQUEST != GRANT. Seeing a tool name in telemetry does not mean coded_policy granted it.
investigations.does_not_prove: A requested_scope value is not authorization. Argument hash is not the raw argument object.
investigations.related_control: CTRL-MCP-001 (you have not read the decision yet)

investigations.title: Find the authorization decision
investigations.security_question: What did CTRL-MCP-001 decide and why?
investigations.learning_objective: CTRL-MCP-001 is the tool PDP. Splunk did not make that decision.
investigations.starter_guidance: Filter event.name=agentsec.control.decision on the same run.id. Read control.id, decision, reason.
investigations.hint_1: The hunt is Q-MCP-AUTHZ. Restrict to event.name=agentsec.control.decision. Control executed stays false on ALLOW.
investigations.hint_2: LIVE ATTACK expect ALLOW with a fail-open reason. Defended RETEST expect DENY tool_not_granted. BASELINE expect ALLOW tool_granted.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Control rows only. BASELINE: ALLOW tool_granted. LIVE ATTACK: ALLOW fail-open. Defended RETEST: DENY tool_not_granted, outcome=prevented.
investigations.result_explanation: decision and reason are runtime fields copied into the index. attempted/executed on this event describe the governed handler at decision time.
investigations.security_interpretation: AcmeBank enforced CTRL-MCP-001 at acmebank.mcp.authorize before the handler. Splunk observed the copy. ALLOW is not execution.
investigations.does_not_prove: DENY by itself does not prove the handler never ran. You still need execution evidence. Splunk is not the enforcement point.

investigations.title: Did the handler start?
investigations.security_question: Is there execution evidence after the authorization decision?
investigations.learning_objective: ALLOW != EXECUTION. mcp.started with executed=true means the handler began. Runtime handler count is authoritative for non-execution.
investigations.starter_guidance: Search mcp.started / mcp.completed / mcp.failed on this run.id. Read has_started on Q-MCP-EXECUTED. Do not read control executed as handler execution.
investigations.hint_1: Q-MCP-TOOL is mcp.started only. Q-MCP-EXECUTED joins control + mcp.* into execution_state.
investigations.hint_2: BASELINE and LIVE ATTACK complete copies: mcp.started then mcp.completed, handler 1. Defended RETEST complete copy: zero mcp.started. Zero Splunk rows corroborate local handler_invoke_count; they do not independently prove prevention.
investigations.expected_result_shape: BASELINE/ATTACK complete copy: has_started=1, execution_state=mcp.completed. Defended RETEST complete copy: has_started=0, execution_state=no_mcp_execution_event.
investigations.result_explanation: mcp.started with executed=true means the handler began. mcp.completed is success of a begun call. mcp.failed is execution then error, not DENY.
investigations.security_interpretation: Prevention is DENY before invoke plus handler_invoke_count=0. Splunk absence of mcp.started is corroboration only.
investigations.does_not_prove: Missing mcp.started is not blocked, SAFE, or prevented if export was incomplete. Do not treat empty Splunk as the control.

investigations.title: What can you prove?
investigations.security_question: Which statements are supported by this evidence, corroborated, not proven, or incorrect?
investigations.learning_objective: Classify claims. DENY is not proof of non-execution by itself. ATTACK is not an alert. Splunk is not enforcement.
investigations.starter_guidance: For each statement, pick: SUPPORTED BY EVIDENCE, CORROBORATED, NOT PROVEN, or INCORRECT. Tie the answer to a field or a pack file.
investigations.hint_1: SUPPORTED needs a runtime or complete indexed field. CORROBORATED is Splunk agreeing with a complete local copy. NOT PROVEN is a gap. INCORRECT contradicts the evidence model.
investigations.hint_2: Refresh: REQUEST != GRANT; ALLOW != EXECUTION; DENY != automatic proof of non-execution; missing event != blocked; Splunk != enforcement; ATTACK != ALERT; 0 DET-MCP-001 rows != SAFE; HEC success != searchable evidence.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Classification exercise. Q-MCP-AFTER-DENY on a complete defended RETEST copy is 0 rows — corroboration, not independent prevention proof. DET-MCP-001 is silent on fail-open ALLOW and on DENY-without-start.
investigations.result_explanation: Q-MCP-AFTER-DENY asks whether mcp.started followed DENY on the same run/tool. Zero rows on a complete copy means that sequence was not indexed. The DETECT tab positive-control table is SIMULATED.
investigations.security_interpretation: You can prove what the complete evidence says. You cannot promote gaps, HEC 200, Studio rendering, or detector silence into prevention.
investigations.does_not_prove: This workshop does not prove INV-001 for other tools, production IAM, or later MCP labs. Zero detection rows are not a new detector.

investigations.title: ATTACK vs RETEST
investigations.security_question: Was the request equivalent, and what security state changed?
investigations.learning_objective: Prove SAME ungranted request, DIFFERENT server-owned defense, DIFFERENT outcome. Splunk observed; Splunk did not cause it.
investigations.starter_guidance: Use the LIVE RUN PAIR from Attack Service. Path A: run Q-MCP-AUTHZ and Q-MCP-EXECUTED twice, once per run.id. Path B: canonical REPLAY tables on COMPARE. Measure the request fingerprint; do not trust fixture names.
investigations.hint_1: SAME: lookup_customer_tier, customer:read, arguments hash, CTRL-MCP-001 placement. DIFFERENT: experiment_id, security.profile, testbed.mode, decision, mcp.started presence.
investigations.hint_2: Authoritative: runtime handler_invoke_count. Control evidence: decision+reason. Corroborative: complete Splunk copy. Not sufficient alone: missing event, DENY string, HEC 200, empty dashboard, pytest.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK: ALLOW fail-open + mcp.started. RETEST: DENY tool_not_granted + 0 mcp.started on a complete copy. Fingerprints match. run.ids differ.
investigations.result_explanation: The experimental variable is the server-owned ExperimentContext. The request fingerprint must match. Empty COMPARE tables on canonical ids mean those UUIDs are not on this volume.
investigations.security_interpretation: AcmeBank changed the outcome by using a different experiment configuration. Splunk reconstructed both copies. Splunk did not ALLOW or DENY.
investigations.does_not_prove: RETEST is not automatically SAFE. DENY is not universal tool-authorization resistance. Missing telemetry is not prevention.
